Veterinary routing, not a generic autoresponder

Different needs deserve different paths.

UrgentEscalate to the clinic’s on-call contact and direct the caller to the clinic’s emergency instructions.
AppointmentCapture the best callback number and time, or send the clinic’s booking link.
RefillPlace the request in the morning refill queue with the caller’s text attached.
OtherKeep the full reply and summarize it for follow-up.
“This sounds urgent.” is useful only if it reaches the right human, right away.

TextTriage applies the escalation rules and emergency wording your clinic approves. It does not diagnose, replace a veterinarian, or replace your emergency phone protocol.

The practical questions

Do we have to replace our phones?

No. TextTriage is designed around conditional call forwarding for busy or unanswered calls, so your existing number and phone system stay in place.

Does TextTriage diagnose emergencies?

No. It detects clinic-approved urgent language and triggers the clinic’s approved instructions and escalation path. It does not provide veterinary diagnosis or replace emergency veterinary care.

What happens after hours?

Your clinic chooses the wording, urgent terms, on-call destination, quiet hours, and emergency instructions. Those rules are tested with your team before the pilot begins.

Does it integrate with our practice software?

No practice-management integration is required for the founding pilot. The first version focuses on the missed-call conversation, routing, escalation, and digest.

When can we start?

TextTriage is currently preparing its founding-clinic pilot. Production messaging will begin only after required carrier registration and clinic approval of the message flow.
